description:
pkix-ct/src/lib.rs:89-94

The `UnsupportedSignatureAlgorithm { hash_alg: u8, sig_alg: u8 }`
variant exposes the wire-format RFC 5246 §7.4.1.4.1 tags directly.
Once shipped, callers can match the variant and extract the raw tag
values — locking the maintainer in.

The struct variant prevents a later cleanup like:

```rust
UnsupportedSignatureAlgorithm(SctAlgorithm)
```

where `SctAlgorithm` is a typed enum, because doing so is a breaking
change for any caller that destructured the inline fields.

`Error` already has `#[non_exhaustive]` on the enum so adding new
variants is fine. But struct variants like this one need their own
`#[non_exhaustive]` to allow adding fields. RFC 5246's hash_alg /
sig_alg space is fixed today, but RFC 8446 deprecated some entries
and added the `SignatureScheme` namespace. If pkix-ct ever wants to
surface "this is actually a `SignatureScheme` from TLS 1.3" the
variant needs more fields.

Recommendation: `#[non_exhaustive]` on the struct-variant fields, OR
wrap the pair in a small typed struct that itself can be extended:

```rust
#[non_exhaustive]
UnsupportedSignatureAlgorithm {
    hash_alg: u8,
    sig_alg: u8,
}
```

Also: same applies to `Error::UnsupportedVersion(u8)` — tuple variant
allows callers to match `Error::UnsupportedVersion(v)`. If the wire
version becomes a typed enum later, that's a breaking change. Less
important because `u8` is the right representation here; just noting.
title: Error::UnsupportedSignatureAlgorithm exposes raw u8 hash_alg/sig_alg — locks RFC 5246 wire encoding
